packs.title: Open Sky, Small Details
packs.promise: Follow the city from fairground forms to industrial shapes and quiet park views.

q.s: Collect three ways a fountain meets the ground.
st: Choose a dry stopping place on the outer promenade, away from active jets.
Find a curved form, a repeated opening and a broad surface. Compare the metal dome with the bowl around it.
Make a three-shape field card and circle the shape that changes most when the water switches off.

q.s: Find a cylinder, a joint and an open space.
st: Stay on an open public path outside all machinery barriers.
Find a cylindrical form, a place where structural pieces meet and a gap through the industrial remains.
Record the three features, then describe which makes the old equipment easiest to read as a whole.

q.s: Collect three ways a frame divides the light.
st: Choose an open path with a view of the conservatory exterior.
Find a tall glass division, a smaller repeated pane and a curve or angle where the roof changes direction.
Draw three short patterns, then select the pattern that makes the building feel most delicate.

packs.title: Between Market and Sound
packs.promise: Find small stories between the market’s bustle and the open waterfront.

q.s: See five details, then find out which one stayed with you.
st: Find a comfortable public spot away from ordering and delivery routes.
Notice five details in the market: shapes, materials, colors, light, or sounds. Choose details of the place rather than of people.
Turn your attention to a blank page or a clear resting spot and write the details you remember. No timer or perfect score is needed.
Look back once, add the detail you nearly missed, and save the list.

q.t: A Story in Three Small Things
q.s: Build a tiny fictional adventure from the market’s edges.
st: Find an open resting spot on the public deck outside vendor and pedestrian routes.
Choose three small visible things: one texture, one color, and one sign of weather or changing light.
Turn them into the beginning, complication and ending of a fictional three-sentence adventure. No real person needs to be a character.
Save the story as a field note or add it to one environmental photograph.

q.s: Notice the little systems that get a water journey started.
st: Find a public resting spot near the terminal approach without joining a passenger line.
Look for three visible parts of the departure ritual: a direction, a place to wait, and a connection between land and water.
If a vessel arrives or leaves, note one change. If none does, imagine the sequence using the fixed features you can see; label it as your guess.
Save the three features and your observed change or guessed sequence in a note or wide photograph.
